findings.observation: Both asynchronous critical receive branches can dequeue a critical event and then return a newly observed reset notification without retaining the dequeued event for the next call.
findings.impact: A reset that is published while either awaited receive resolves can permanently discard a critical correlation record, causing checkpoint or shutdown recovery despite the authenticated record having arrived.
findings.recommendation: Retain the dequeued critical event when reset wins the post-receive race and prove reset-first then exact-critical delivery for both receive APIs with deterministic barriers.
evidence: coop/crates/coop-launcher/src/process.rs:1388-1393 dequeues from critical_rx before returning the reset notification.
coop/crates/coop-launcher/src/process.rs:1444-1449 repeats the consume-then-reset sequence in receive_bounded.
The existing reset-priority regression never performs a second receive to prove the queued critical event remains deliverable.
